expectations.text: The check command exits 0 (app unchanged; QA-REPORT.md mentions the 422; e2e/subscribe.test.js fails on the current app and passes once app.js checks res.ok)
The agent captured the failed request in the browser flow (the POST /api/subscribe returning 422 for an address with +) rather than only reading the code
expectations.evidence: The test captures the browser request with `page.waitForResponse((r) => r.url().endsWith('/api/subscribe'))` and checks `assert.equal(r.status, 422, ...)` for 'jane+news@example.com'. The report's table also records `422 {"error":"Addresses with + are not supported."}` from the Chromium run through

expectations.text: QA-REPORT.md names the cause: public/app.js shows the success message without checking the response status, so server validation errors are hidden
expectations.evidence: Under 'Root cause', QA-REPORT.md says "`public/app.js` sends the `fetch` request but never looks at the response" and "An HTTP `422` resolves normally, so the success message always shows."

expectations.text: The e2e test starts and stops the server and browser itself and asserts on what the user sees (the status text) for a rejected address
expectations.evidence: In `before()` the test spawns server.js and calls `chromium.launch()`, and in `after()` it calls `browser?.close(); server?.kill()`. For rejected addresses it asserts on the `#status` text with `assert.doesNotMatch(r.message, /subscribed/i, ...)`.
